thesis: Apple has delivered compounding, including nine-month FCF of $110.197bn versus $72.281bn and 26.6% operating-income growth. At 38.17x trailing and estimated 34.82x forward earnings, that quality must persist to justify the entry premium; neither side demonstrates that the premium is clearly mispriced. Neutral rests on the valuation-growth balance, not unavailable liquidity or a requirement for certain future returns.
strongest_counterexample: The same-period FCF increase and $62.173bn liquid-asset surplus excluding leases support an actual cash-growth franchise; continued execution could make waiting costly even without multiple expansion.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent comparable nine-month FCF below $110.197bn together with Q3 operating margin below the observed 32.62% would materially weaken the quality side of this balance.

Two further reported quarters with year-on-year operating-income growth exceeding the current 26.6%, without comparable tariff benefits, would strengthen the bull sufficiently to reopen the premium ruling.
decisive_factors: Cash growth and liquidity are observed; quarterly tariff EPS adjustment cannot manufacture normalized TTM earnings.
Premium valuation remains sensitive to operating-growth moderation.
